messages:
alice: quick heads-up — our SDK CI started failing on the `pip install .` step for the py package. local `poetry install` works fine. CI log says 'Failed building wheel for redwood-client' and then later mypy complains about missing type info. anyone seen this combo before?
ben: can you paste the exact error snippet? often this is a wheel-build vs build-backend mismatch or missing `py.typed`. ci log link: https://ci.internal/12345 (if public perms)
achch: i'm not chris but another quick Q: are we using poetry's default build backend? (PEP 517)
alice: error shows: `error: subprocess-exited-with-error\n× Building wheel for redwood-client (pyproject.toml) did not run successfully.` then later `note: Skipping analyzing redwood_client (no library stub or py.typed)` — so mypy falls back.
ben: common fixes in order: 1) make sure package includes `py.typed` so mypy knows it's typed; add it to package_data or include in sdist/wheel. 2) in CI, use poetry export to produce a deterministic constraints file and install with pip -c. this avoids building from source variability. e.g.:
```bash
poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o ci/constraints.txt
pip install -c ci/constraints.txt .[async]
```
that will pin exact transitive deps in CI.
chris: also double-check pyproject.toml has a build backend like `build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"` (poetry core) under `[build-system]`. if CI image is missing `poetry-core` pip will try to build and fail. adding `python -m pip install build poetry-core` early in job helps.
dana: separate but related — some async streaming tests are failing with `RuntimeError: This event loop is already running` when we run pytest in GH actions. locally fine. any tips?
ben: for pytest + async streaming use `pytest-asyncio` (or `anyio`) and mark tests `@pytest.mark.asyncio` and ensure GH runner doesn't try to run event loop twice. in GH actions use `pytest -q` with `python -m pip install pytest-asyncio` and in `pytest.ini` set:
```ini
[pytest]
asyncio_mode = auto
```
then use patterns like:
```python
async def test_streaming(client):
    async for chunk in client.stream_chat(...):
        assert "choices" in chunk
    await client.aclose()  # ensure cleanup
```
if tests spawn loop inside threads, switch to `anyio` backend.
emma: from infra side — the reliable CI pattern we've been using for wheels: 1) `python -m pip install --upgrade pip build wheel` 2) `python -m build -w` to produce wheels in `dist/` 3) `pip install dist/*.whl` in a later step. that eliminates on-the-fly builds on the runner. if your package uses C-extensions/requires manylinux, use our internal wheelhouse or `cibuildwheel` in release pipeline.
chris: extra on typing: publish `py.typed` and add `typing-extensions` in `pyproject` extras for older python support. also add `package.__init__.__all__`? (less relevant) and ensure `mypy.ini` points to libs. if you want stub-only approach, ship `types-redwood-client` but that's overkill.
alice: ok i'll try the `poetry export` -> `pip install -c` route first and make sure `py.typed` is included in package. also will add the build step to CI to create wheels and install from `dist/`.
ben: one more small note — Poetry's lock files can cause pinned markers that conflict with some runners' platform tags. using `--without-hashes` and exporting for the target platform is safest.
ci-bot: CI job #12345 rerun by @alice — https://ci.internal/12345/runs/67890 :white_check_mark:
alice: perfect, i'll push a branch with changes and ping for a quick review. thanks all :thumbsup:
ben: feel free to @ben if you want me to add the CI steps to the shared pipeline template.
chris: i'll pair on adding `py.typed` packaging change if you want.
dana: if streaming tests still flake, drop me the failing job and i'll capture the event loop trace.
emma: noting action item: update ci-template to include wheel-build step (tracked).
alice: closing thread after i open PR, will paste link. thanks everyone! :pray:
